title: Value vs Reference Types: C# Core Idea

scenes.say: Ever wonder why C Sharp separates structs and classes? Let's break down why value versus reference types matter for every engineer.

scenes.label: Struct
scenes.sub: Stores its data directly. Copied on assignment.
scenes.say: A struct is a value type. When you assign it, the data gets copied. It's fast and lives on the stack.

scenes.label: Class
scenes.sub: Holds a reference to data on the heap.
scenes.say: A class is a reference type. Assigning it copies the reference, not the data itself. The actual data sits on the heap.
So, structs hold their data directly. Classes just point to it. That's a big difference for performance and bugs.

scenes.code:
int x = 5;
object o = x; // boxing
scenes.say: When you assign a value type like an int to an object, C Sharp boxes it. That means wrapping the value in a reference type, which adds overhead.

scenes.question: Are records value types?
scenes.right: No, records are reference types with value-based equality.
scenes.say: Don't mix this up: records look like value types, but they're actually reference types optimized for immutability and equality.
